subject: Re: Hosted API minimum / spike cap & on-demand surcharge
messages:
From: alex.jensen@northscale.com
To: vanessa.ortiz@redwood.ai
Cc: procurement@northscale.com
Date: Tue, 10 Nov 2026 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Hosted API — minimum commit + spike protection question

Vanessa — thanks for the run-through today. Quick follow up from procurement and engineering: we like the proposed monthly commit but need clarity on two operational points before I can circulate internally:

1) If we commit to $150k/month, what is the per-token overage rate when we spike beyond the commit? Do you offer an intermediate on-demand surcharge (e.g., 1.25x of on-demand rate) or a flat overage per-token?

2) Our traffic pattern is bursty (daily spikes up to ~3x baseline for short windows). Can Redwood provide a "spike cap" or short-term budget cap that prevents runaway charges without throttling requests? If so, how is that priced or configured?

Also attaching an internal MAP sheet — procurement asked for list pricing vs committed pricing rows.

Appreciate any sample language we could drop into purchase order or SOW.

—Alex
Alex Jensen
Head of Platform, NorthScale
From: vanessa.ortiz@redwood.ai
To: alex.jensen@northscale.com
Cc: ben.carter@redwood.ai, kimberly.park@redwood.ai
Date: Wed, 11 Nov 2026 10:03:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Hosted API — minimum commit + spike protection question

Alex — thanks, this is helpful context. Quick answers and a proposed option we use with other scale customers:

- Overage pricing: For a $150k/month commit we typically set a two-tier overage path. Normal on-demand (pay-as-you-go) token rate = $0.0008/token. Overage if you exceed commit in a month = on-demand rate * 0.95 (i.e., a slight discount) up to a soft cap. For short emergency bursts beyond a configured "spike cap" we can apply a surcharge of 1.2x on the on-demand rate. That surcharge is to disincentivize sustained overage but still permit short spikes.

- Spike cap: Redwood can set a short-window spike cap (configurable by time window, e.g., 15m/1h) that will route excess requests to an on-demand queue with the surcharge applied. The customer can choose to either allow the surcharge route (requests served but billed higher) or opt for hard-throttle once the cap is hit.

Proposed SKU for NorthScale:
- Monthly commit: $150,000 (hosted API)
- Baseline per-token above commit (true-up): $0.00076/token (5% discount on on-demand)
- Short-window spike surcharge: on-demand * 1.2 = $0.00096/token for minutes-long bursts beyond spike cap
- Spike cap default: 3x baseline QPS for any rolling 15-minute window (can be tuned).

I've attached the updated pricing PDF with sample language for the PO (section 4.2) and a suggested paragraph for surge-handling. If that looks fine, I can loop in legal for an amendment.

—Vanessa
Vanessa Ortiz
Head of Sales, Redwood Inference

Notes for commercial: two points to consider before we commit to the 1.2x surcharge:

1) Competitive comparables: most enterprise customers prefer either a capped surcharge (1.1–1.25x) OR a true-up with flexible burst credits. If NorthScale wants predictable monthly spend, offering a modest bank of burst credits (e.g., 100M tokens/mo) that reset monthly may be cleaner than per-minute surcharging. This reduces helpdesk escalations.

2) Implementation: spike cap enforcement requires dashboard controls and billing hooks so the customer can see spike usage in near real-time. We should include a UI toggle in the Console for NorthScale to switch between throttle/surcharge/credits. Geoff in product needs to ack on timeline (2–4 weeks to expose controls).

If they want the burst credits alternative, margin math still keeps us profitable if we price credits at ~0.9x of on-demand.

—Ben
From: kimberly.park@redwood.ai

Alex — quick legal wording you can drop into the SOW or PO for the surge handling clause:

"Surge Handling and Overage: Customer may configure short-window surge caps in the Redwood Console. When a configured surge cap is exceeded, Redwood will either (a) route excess requests to an on-demand ingress queue and bill at the on-demand rate multiplied by the agreed surge multiplier, or (b) hard-throttle requests when the Customer elects throttling in writing. Surge multipliers and caps shall be set forth in the Order Form. Redwood will provide near-real-time usage metrics and notify Customer when surge thresholds are reached."
We recommend leaving the choice of surcharge vs. throttle to NorthScale and including the burst-credit alternative as a schedule. If you'd like, I can produce a short amendment template.

—Kimberly
Legal Counsel, Redwood Inference

- Provide a price for a monthly burst credit bundle (we suggested 100M tokens) and an alternate price for a larger 500M token bundle.
